title: The Hard Lessons That Transformed Our Careers — Harvard & Stanford Grads Reveal
summary: A 2025 year-end recap in which the sisters reflect on becoming the number one business show on Spotify, appearing on a Penn Station billboard as a Spotify RADAR creator, and the lessons behind that growth. Key takeaways: dream bigger and leave room for serendipity, run the podcast like a product with relentless experimentation, invest in professional brand identity earlier than feels comfortable, act as curators of guests and content, be highly selective about sponsors, and keep going because women of color hosting business podcasts is a stark white space.

ideas.idea: High achievers who try to control every outcome leave no room for serendipity; keep imagining things bigger than you can plan a ladder to.
ideas.detail: Jean kept joking 'wait until they see me on a billboard' and in 2025 Spotify put Tiger Sisters on a digital billboard at Penn Station as one of about five US RADAR podcast creators. Cherie says it was not even on her vision board and the lesson is she needs to dream bigger.

ideas.idea: A physical manifestation of digital work carries outsized meaning, and representation matters: two Asian women on a business-podcast billboard felt like breaking new ground.
ideas.detail: Cherie could not name any peers in tech or business who had been on a billboard, and the sisters framed it as a milestone symbolizing the year's growth in a world where everything they make is digital.

ideas.idea: Tiger Sisters grew fast in one year because the sisters run the podcast like product managers: relentless experimentation, reading every comment, keeping what works and shedding what does not.
ideas.detail: Seasons 3 through 6 each looked different: season 3 was the first all-interview season (filmed standing up, which viewers found awkward), they moved from the office to a living-room set in season 5, ran an AMA from the Spotify studio in New York, and bought Aputure 300D II lights for season 6. Jean has 12-13 years in product, Cherie over 5.

ideas.idea: Platform partners advise 'don't change too much', but take that with a grain of salt when experimentation is your DNA.
ideas.detail: Spotify and YouTube partners cautioned against changing the format, yet the hosts credit adaptability and the same experimentation mindset they use in their careers and personal lives for the show's growth.

ideas.idea: Launch with an MVP, but know when to level up and hire a talented specialist; the sisters wish they had invested in a professional rebrand sooner.
ideas.detail: The original blue podcast cover was a photo-booth picture with no photographer. For season 6 they did a styled shoot at the Albright Fashion Library with designer Emily Sims, calling it 'the best money we've ever spent'; the new art stands out visually on the business and tech charts.

ideas.idea: Stay in every detail of your brand rather than handing it to an agency, so the result feels true to who you are.
ideas.detail: The hosts were involved in colors, outfits, and how the older-sister/younger-sister duality came through in the rebrand; it cost a lot of time and energy but 'you can feel Jean and me in the rebrand'.

ideas.idea: In a world of AI slop where anyone can be a podcast host, the value is in being a trusted curator who finds the signal in the noise.
ideas.detail: The hosts read widely, talk to many people, and see themselves as curators of both content and voices, aiming to be the signal their audience trusts to deliver the right content at the right time.

ideas.idea: Every guest has come organically through the sisters' network, never cold outreach, so the through line across varied guests is the hosts themselves as curators.
ideas.detail: Guests are 'nerd Hollywood': niche celebrities like billionaire real-estate and startup investor Fernando De Leon (a personal friend who built himself from nothing) and the Rabil brothers, founders of the Premier Lacrosse League who raised over $100 million, connected via Cherie's Dartmouth network. The ethos is sharing the one-on-one coffee chats they would otherwise have privately.

ideas.idea: Hold off on sponsors until the product is right, then start selling to people you already know and whose companies your audience has met.
ideas.detail: Jean's first-ever sponsor outreach was a June 12 text to four former guests; David Shim, co-founder and CEO of Read AI, replied immediately because they were about to begin marketing for the first time, becoming the show's first brand partner.

ideas.idea: Audience trust is a creator's most important asset, so vet every sponsor for fit with your mission and only read ads you can stand behind.
ideas.detail: The hosts decline many inbound sponsor requests for fit, timing or diligence reasons. Cherie, with over five years in content creation, says many creators just 'need to get a check' but partner selection requires conscience, ethics and discernment.

ideas.idea: Two Asian American women hosting a top business and tech podcast is an extreme statistical white space, roughly 0.0225 percent, which makes continuing the show feel imperative.
ideas.detail: A USC Annenberg study found 8 percent of business and tech podcasts are hosted by women and 7 percent of the top 100 podcasts are hosted by women of color; male hosts also book more male guests, so fewer women's voices get platformed overall.
names_or_cases: USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism

ideas.idea: Apple's top 2025 episodes show huge demand for women's topics like perimenopause and female identity, but mostly from male podcasters, proving an underserved market for women speaking to women.
ideas.detail: Cherie's takeaway: 'we don't need another bro podcaster asking about women's health, we need more women talking about women's issues,' and the goal is an ecosystem where female business voices reach parity rather than one or two in the top ten.

ideas.idea: Do a year-end reflection listing your top five to eight wins and lessons, since a win and a lesson often come together.
ideas.detail: The hosts model this by framing each 2025 highlight (billboard, rebrand, first sponsor) as both a win and a lesson, and invite listeners to share their number one win or takeaway.
